ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-03-15
Provider: Dr. James O'Brien, MD
Department: Emergency Medicine
Visit Type: ed

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
3-day history of increasing left breast pain, swelling, fever, and chills in breastfeeding mother

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient is a 30-year-old female with primary adrenal insufficiency evaluated for right breast pain earlier today, and presents to the emergency department with a 3-day history of increasing pain and swelling in her left breast. She reports fever and chills since yesterday. She is breastfeeding her 2-month-old infant.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Normal spontaneous vaginal delivery (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Second-degree perineal tear (healed) (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Nipple fissure due to improper breastfeeding technique (diagnosed 2020-02-15)
- Primary adrenal insufficiency (diagnosed 2020-03-15)
- Mastitis (diagnosed 2020-03-15)
- Diastasis recti abdominis

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Repair of second-degree perineal tear (first delivery)
- Spontaneous vaginal delivery x2

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Hydrocortisone 20 mg PO qAM, 10 mg PO qPM
- Fludrocortisone 0.1 mg PO daily

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Autoimmune hypothyroidism (mother)
- Rheumatoid arthritis (maternal aunt)
- Type 1 diabetes mellitus (paternal cousin)

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None (breastfeeding). Occupation: Elementary school teacher.

VITAL SIGNS:
Temperature is 38.7°C (101.7°F), heart rate is 102 beats per minute, and blood pressure is 120/78 mmHg

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
The left breast is erythematous and edematous with a 5 cm fluctuant mass noted in the upper outer quadrant. There is associated tenderness on palpation and axillary lymphadenopathy on the same side. The right breast appears normal.

LABORATORY DATA:
White blood cell count: 14,000/mm³ (normal 4,500-11,000/mm³)
- Hemoglobin: 13.2 g/dL (normal 12-16 g/dL)
- C-reactive protein: 24 mg/L (normal <5 mg/L)

Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Persistent bilateral nipple pain and abrasions while breastfeeding 1-month-old infant

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient is a 30-year-old female with primary adrenal insufficiency and diastasis recti abdominis who returns approximately one month following normal spontaneous vaginal delivery. She presents with persistent breastfeeding difficulties. She describes the pain as sharp and burning, which worsens during feeding. She also reports bilateral nipple abrasions and occasional bloody nipple discharge. The patient has been exclusively breastfeeding and has not introduced bottle feeding. The patient is concerned about the possibility of infection or underlying breast pathology.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Normal spontaneous vaginal delivery (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Second-degree perineal tear (healed) (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Primary adrenal insufficiency
- Diastasis recti abdominis

Her pregnancy was uncomplicated, and she had a normal spontaneous vaginal delivery.

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Repair of second-degree perineal tear (first delivery)
- Spontaneous vaginal delivery x2

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Hydrocortisone 20 mg PO qAM, 10 mg PO qPM
- Fludrocortisone 0.1 mg PO daily

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Autoimmune hypothyroidism (mother)
- Rheumatoid arthritis (maternal aunt)
- Type 1 diabetes mellitus (paternal cousin)

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None (breastfeeding). Occupation: Elementary school teacher.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS:
She denies any fever, chills, or flu-like symptoms.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On physical examination, the nipples are erythematous with small cracks, but there is no evidence of mastitis or breast engorgement. No masses are palpable, and the infant appears well-nourished and active.
